data.claim: The premise is stale: the code, the editable install and the project stamp are all 0.2.11, the upgrade 0.2.10 to 0.2.11 was already applied 2026-11-11T05:23, and the plan now holds 3 items, not 239. Nothing structural remains to apply.
data.falsifier: ddflow upgrade --plan run in the primary checkout reports more than 3 pending items, or ddflow --version differs from ddflow/__init__.py
data.mechanism: ddflow on PATH is $HOME/.local/bin/ddflow, a shell wrapper that runs python -m ddflow from the development checkout (.venv, editable install, version from ddflow/__init__.py, DDFLOW_HOME override); so there is no pipx or uv tool copy to upgrade and the code is always the checkout's HEAD. The 'config is newer than this code' warning is emitted by ddflow/config/_warn.py when a tree whose code is older than its config (a worktree on an old base, or an agent started before the stamp moved) skips unknown keys; it is cured by merging main into that tree, not by upgrade --apply. Pending plan: (1) repair forced-completions, 57 findings, agent-applicable, annotates the log only; (2) repair unknown-author-shards, 7 shards, needs operator --confirm with --reason; (3) instructions: docs/ddflow/drivers/deltas/claude-code.md hand-edited, refreshed by ddflow adopt --refresh-docs keeping .local-edits. Risks: the two repairs append events to the log (no schema change, no new strict-fold kind), no MCP tool change, no hook change, no pin change in the plan. Agents still on older versions (0.1.x to 0.2.10 per upgrade --status) must restart to pick up 0.2.11 code and MCP tools. Rollback: backups exist under .ddflow/backups (20261111T035500679118Z-0.2.10-to-0.2.10); ddflow upgrade --restore NAME, or --snapshot for a git tag; event appends are not reversible except by git revert of the events commit. Order and moment: merge main into stale worktrees first, let the current lanes merge, run upgrade --plan again, then --apply repairs, confirm the shard authors after git log review, then adopt --refresh-docs, then restart agents.

The 239-item count could not be reproduced here; it was probably seen from a project or tree whose stamp is older (another repository using the same wrapper, or a stale worktree).
